deadline.value: No single funding deadline. Advertised projects (funded or unfunded) carry their own deadlines, and a self-proposed application can be made at any time. JARSS studentships are applied for by supervisors, with departmental internal deadlines; the JARSS page still describes the 2026/27 round (deadlines as early as late 2025), so contact the department early.
deadline.quote: There are two main routes to undertaking a research project at Strathclyde - either by applying for an existing project or pursuing your own specific areas of interest. | You can apply at any time – all you have to do is pick your course and submit your application.

also.quote: Academics/Supervisors make the applications for this scheme and there are various deadlines across Departments and Faculties, therefore, in the first instance, all interested applicants should contact the Department where they would like to carry out their research.

app_fee.value: Not stated on the pages checked

fee_waiver.value: Not stated on the pages checked

toefl_min.value: Physics PGR needs IELTS 6.5 (Faculty of Science PGR: no band below 5.5). Equivalent TOEFL iBT for tests up to Jan 20, 2026: 80 overall (L17, R18, S20, W18); tests from Jan 21, 2026: 5.0 overall with at least 4.0 in each component.
toefl_min.quote: English Condition - IELTS condition 6.5 overall, with a minimum of 5.5 in each component | TOEFL (ibt): Tests dated up to and including 20th January, 2026: 80 overall, with the following minimum scores in each component: Listening: 17 Reading: 18 Speaking: 20 Writing: 18. Tests dated from 21st January, 2026: 5.0 overall, with a minimum of 4.0 in each component.

also.quote: Faculty of Science (PGR students): IELTS (Academic) 6.5 overall (no individual band less than 5.5)
You must also have an IELTS score of 6.5 as proof of English proficiency, if English isn't your first language.

english_waiver.value: Not stated on the pages checked (no India-specific or medium-of-instruction exemption found on the English requirements pages)

supervisor.value: You can contact a supervisor before applying, or name who you would like to work with; your proposal is then passed to potential supervisors, and an offer follows once a second supervisor is confirmed. For JARSS funding, supervisors make the application, so contact the department or supervisor first.
supervisor.quote: You can identify and interact with a supervisor before applying, or you can let us know who you'd like to work within your application and we'll team you up with the best supervisor for your project. When we've received your application, your research proposal is passed to potential supervisors for consideration.

also.quote: Applications are made by academic supervisors and, in the first instance, interested candidates should contact the Department/Supervisor they are interested in working with.

funding.value: Funding is project by project; many listed physics projects are unfunded. JARSS (about 100 studentships university-wide) is open to international fee status but its stated value is home fees plus a UKRI-rate stipend.
funding.quote: Projects don't always have funding attached to them. If this is the case, find out ways to fund your research.

also.quote: Number of scholarships: 100 | Value: Home fees and stipend at UKRI rate | England or N. Ireland or Rep. Ireland or Wales, Home (Scottish), International

entry_route.value: Physics page: a master's or integrated master's in physics, or a first or 2:1 UK honours degree (or overseas equivalent). The University's India entry guidance says research-degree applicants would normally need a master's and some research experience, so Indian bachelor's-only applicants should check with the department.
entry_route.quote: You require to have one of the following: | Masters or an Integrated Masters Degree in physics | first-class or upper second-class UK Honours degree, or overseas equivalent, from a recognised educational establishment in physics

also.quote: If you wish to apply for a research degree you'd normally have to have a Masters degree and some experience of research work.

notes: International PhD tuition was £29,350 for 2026/27 (2027/28 not yet listed on the page checked). A research proposal of 250 to 1,000 words is required.
